blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-migration-1 (Account field renamed in the public API without a BREAKING mark or a transition) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-migration-2 (Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no down migration or backup step) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: `Account` is a type of the public HTTP API (src/api.rs:1); every existing client that reads `user_name` from the account endpoint gets a missing field after deploy, with no warning. Mark it **BREAKING** in the proposal's release note (today it reads "Changed: Account JSON uses camelCase.") with what clients must do, and give consumers time: serialize both `user_name` (deprecated) and `userName` for a release, or version the endpoint, before removing the snake_case field.
findings.title: Account field renamed in the public API without a BREAKING mark or a transition

findings.evidence: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email;
findings.recommendation: Running 0005 on production deletes every stored `legacy_email` value for good: there is no `0005_drop_legacy_email.down.sql` (0004 has one), and neither the plan nor the tasks back up the column. Add a backup step (copy `id, legacy_email` to an archive table or dump) and a down migration that re-adds the column and restores it, or state in the plan why the data can be lost and how to recover.
findings.title: Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no down migration or backup step
